strokeOrderSource.variation: The independent-form handwriting animation draws the full be-series bowl first in one uninterrupted right-to-left run, then places the left dot above the main line and the right dot beside it: three strokes separated by two pen lifts. The adjacent prose identifies te as the be-series shape with two dots side by side above the main line and notes that handwritten pairs of dots may be replaced by a squiggle or horizontal line. This learner path preserves the explicit two-dot independent form and fits the body-first, three-run order to the course's vendored Noto Naskh fallback; Urdu is conventionally printed in Nastaliq, and the app's true Nastaliq face remains separate from this canonical script-data fallback. The provenance remains Urdu-specific rather than borrowing the separate Arabic or Persian ت sources.
